updates.name: Teak
updates.prompt:
CHANGE ONLY THE HAIR COLOR.

IDENTITY LOCK
Preserve the subject's complete facial identity exactly. Do not alter facial features, expression, skin texture, pores, skin tone, jawline, bone structure, facial proportions, eyes, eyebrows, nose, lips, cheeks, forehead, ears, neck, body, clothing or background.

GEOMETRY LOCK
Preserve the existing haircut and hairstyle exactly: same length, perimeter, silhouette, density, layers, bangs, parting, curl/wave pattern, texture, volume, direction and overall shape. The skull is a rigid fixed object. Only the hair pigment changes.

EAR LOCK
Ear shape locked â€” do not regenerate, reshape, enlarge, reduce, reposition, or reconstruct the ears.

PHOTOGRAPHIC PRESERVATION
Preserve the original framing, crop, camera perspective, focus, lighting direction, exposure, white balance, contrast, color balance, camera grain and noise. No relighting, face retouching, skin grading or background changes.
TARGET COLOR - Teak
Render a salon-realistic Teak: a deep muted teak-wood brown: rich medium-deep brown with restrained warm wood undertones, balanced between neutral brown and soft amber, low-to-moderate saturation, deep but not blackened, with natural darker fiber variation.
Apply the target pigment through the visible hair mass with coherent tonal depth, natural fiber-to-fiber variation and realistic root-to-length continuity. Read the source scalp and existing hairline first; preserve natural scalp emergence and the original root architecture. Do not invent an unrelated dark-root effect or erase legitimate source root architecture. The target color must remain confined to hair.

HAIR-ONLY INTEGRATION
The recolor must follow individual strands, existing texture and original hair boundaries. Preserve natural density, root emergence, flyaways, edge softness, contact shadows and depth. No wig effect, hard mask, halo, painted surface, synthetic uniformity or flat overlay.

ANTI-LIGHTENING SKIN CONTROL
Actively resist any model tendency to lighten, desaturate, warm, cool or otherwise reinterpret the original skin tone while changing hair color. Skin must remain at the same apparent tone, depth, texture and local contrast as the source photograph.
PHOTOGRAPHIC COLOR-REFLECTION / GLOBAL-GRADE LOCK
The target pigment must not recolor or cast visible brown, amber, copper, rose, pink, coral, platinum, lavender, blue, silver or other target-color reflections onto the forehead, cheeks, nose, ears, neck or other skin. Preserve original local highlights, shadows and neutral skin response. Do not use the target hair color as a global photo color grade, warm/cool filter, ambient tint or exposure reinterpretation.
SPECULAR / HIGHLIGHT CONTROL
Highlights and specular response must come from the original light interacting with real hair fibers. Do not invent metallic, neon, fluorescent, plastic, painted or uniformly glossy highlights. Preserve realistic strand-level highlight variation, pigment depth and shadow behavior appropriate to the requested color.
NEGATIVE COLOR COLLISIONS
Do not drift toward auburn, copper, orange, red-brown, burgundy, chocolate-black, golden blonde, caramel, neon brown or flat opaque brown. Do not change the haircut, hair texture, length, volume, parting or silhouette.

REALISM STANDARD
The final image must read as the same original photograph with only the hair pigment changed: physically plausible hair fibers, believable roots, natural tonal variation, original photographic response, and zero facial or environmental color contamination. Image generation and image QA have not been performed at this stage.
